be-0VLo.title: Google car: low smallcam, wide round blur
be-0VLo.summary: The newer Gen 4 smallcam sits lower than normal and has a big round blur with a small bump at the front. It can be see-through. Most of Western Europe has it.

be-0Xu1.title: Landscape: very flat polders with waterways
be-0Xu1.summary: Extremely flat reclaimed fields at or below sea level, cut by many canals, near the North Sea and the western Netherlands border. Often confused with the Netherlands, so look for other clues.

differs.how: Very similar landscape, use signs or road lines

be-3Ooh.title: Signposts: orange posts and orange backs
be-3Ooh.summary: Signposts are often orange, and the backs of signs are sometimes orange too. This is unique.

be-3xpW.title: Sign: small priority sign with orange diamond
be-3xpW.summary: The priority road sign has an orange diamond and is much smaller than elsewhere.

be-5MIw.title: Sign: town entry white with black border
be-5MIw.summary: Town entry signs are white with a black border and the town name in bold black text.

be-5jYM.title: Street sign: varied, short and tall
be-5jYM.summary: Street name signs vary a lot by city, mostly white or dark blue, and usually carry the town name. They are fairly short and tall, while Dutch ones are much longer than tall.

differs.how: Street signs are much longer than they are tall

be-6AkT.title: Coast: wall of apartment blocks, dunes
be-6AkT.summary: Much of the North Sea coast is lined with apartment blocks like a wall. You may also see dunes with low bushes and long grass.

be-6eFr.title: Road: gutters on both sides
be-6eFr.summary: Nearly all roads, big or small, have gutters on both sides. This is much rarer in neighbouring countries.

be-73Bz.title: Chevron: white with a red arrow
be-73Bz.summary: White chevrons with a red arrow. The Netherlands uses the same one, but France does not.

differs.how: France does not use this chevron

be-9KhQ.title: Bus stop: yellow signposts and roofs
be-9KhQ.summary: Bus stops are always marked by yellow signposts, and bus shelters often have yellow roofs.

be-AXSi.title: Plate: red characters
be-AXSi.summary: Plates use red letters and numbers. You can spot the colour even through the blur.

be-Bf5S.title: Sign: crossing with two dotted lines
be-Bf5S.summary: The pedestrian crossing sign has no stripes, just two horizontal dotted lines, and the man has a square head. France and the Netherlands show a zebra crossing with five stripes.

differs.how: Sign shows a zebra crossing with five stripes
Sign shows a zebra crossing with five stripes

be-EGhx.title: Phone numbers: area code after the 0
be-EGhx.summary: Numbers have 9 digits, and the one or two digits after the 0 give the area. Big cities use 0X XXX XX XX, other towns 0XX XX XX XX. Mobiles start with 04 and have 10 digits.

be-IlY6.title: Kilometre marker: green, sometimes red text
be-IlY6.summary: Kilometre markers are often green, and can have red text.

be-Iq0Z.title: Landscape: steep hills, dense forests, valleys
be-Iq0Z.summary: A hilly, wooded area with valleys in the southeast. The same hills continue into France, Luxembourg and Germany.

differs.how: Same hill range continues into Luxembourg
Same hill range continues into France
Same hill range continues into Germany

be-LF07.title: Bollard: white with yellow rectangle, or brown
be-LF07.summary: A white bollard with a yellow rectangular reflector on the front, white on the back, or a dark brown one with two red stripes on top. The brown type also appears in the Netherlands.

differs.how: Danish white bollards have a red top stripe and a non-rectangular reflector

be-Qz6K.title: Houses: grey stone, French look
be-Qz6K.summary: In the south, houses use a lot of stone, have grey tones and look more French.

be-U0Ti.title: Language: Dutch, French or German by region
be-U0Ti.summary: Dutch in the north (lots of z, w, ee, ij), French in the south (ç, é, è, à), and German in a small eastern area (ä, ü, ö, ß).

be-UD8T.title: Pole: square concrete, tiny holes, metal bands
be-UD8T.summary: Square concrete poles with tiny holes running up them and small metal wrappings. The second most common type has oval holes. France has the metal wrappings too.

be-VtiH.title: Street sign: municipality name on the sign
be-VtiH.summary: Street signs often show the municipality name in smaller type than the street. One big tourist city is an exception and usually leaves it out.

be-Wopz.title: Sign: both French and Dutch on signs
be-Wopz.summary: The capital is bilingual, so signs show both French and Dutch.

be-aGFv.title: Guardrail: A-type with yellow reflectors
be-aGFv.summary: A-type guardrail with yellow reflectors. In Europe only Spain, Andorra and Belgium use yellow ones.

be-ahrj.title: Sign: small extra blue plate under road signs
be-ahrj.summary: Road signs often carry an extra small blue plate. Other European countries usually use white ones.

be-by58.title: Road lines: short dashed edges on bike paths
be-by58.summary: Bicycle paths are edged with short dashed lines.

be-ecIc.title: Road: rural roads made of concrete slabs
be-ecIc.summary: Many country roads are made of concrete slabs, like in the Philippines or Thailand. The Netherlands almost never does this.

differs.how: Almost never has concrete slab roads

be-fihD.title: Border: small white crosses on the ground
be-fihD.summary: A town made of many mixed pieces of two countries shows small white crosses on the ground at borders. Street name signs tell you which country you are in.

differs.how: Street name signs show the Dutch side

be-lm-783088.title: Language: Dutch with ij, ieuw, oe and straat
be-lm-783088.summary: Dutch has many double vowels and letter groups like ij, ieuw and oe. The word for street is straat. It is the main language of the north and shares Brussels with French.

differs.how: Same language, so use other clues

be-lm-783090.title: Language: French with rue and accents
be-lm-783090.summary: French uses accents like é, à, è, â, ê, ç and the ending -ux. The word for street is rue. It is spoken in the south and, with Dutch, in Brussels.

differs.how: Same language, so use other clues

be-m1Lx.title: Warning sign: thick red outline, no white edge
be-m1Lx.summary: In the north and Brussels, 95% of warning signs have a thick red outline with no white border. In the south they usually have a thin white edge. The northern ones match Spain's.

be-n3uG.title: Sign: red water hydrant sign with letter H
be-n3uG.summary: A red hydrant sign with the letter H on top. Germany has these too.

be-nGOp.title: Road lines: all white, bike lanes on both sides
be-nGOp.summary: All road lines are white, continuous or broken, and roads often have a bike lane on each side. This is even more common in the Netherlands.

be-npN9.title: Pole: striped traffic light poles
be-npN9.summary: Traffic lights are mostly held by black-and-yellow or red-and-white striped poles. Which one you see depends on the region.

be-rJDM.title: Sign: blue or white direction signs
be-rJDM.summary: Direction signs are most often blue or white.

be-rJaC.title: Pole: yellow-and-black traffic light poles
be-rJaC.summary: Traffic lights on yellow-and-black poles are only found in the north. The south and Brussels often use red-and-white poles.

be-t75X.title: Bus stop sign: white top or yellow top
be-t75X.summary: Bus stop signs have a white rectangle at the top in the north and in Brussels, and a yellow top in the south.

be-u60n.title: Houses: many blurred
be-u60n.summary: Lots of houses are blurred. Only Germany has more blurred houses.

be-uyob.title: Google car: red car with long antenna
be-uyob.summary: A red car with a long antenna is rarely seen here. It is far more common in Ukraine.

be-vR5K.title: Landscape: flat northwest, hillier southeast
be-vR5K.summary: Flat in the northwest, especially near the coast, and gets hillier the further southeast you go.

be-xzJZ.title: Houses: red brick
be-xzJZ.summary: Many houses are built of distinctive red brick, more so in the north and west.
